# gate rows are compared with. It runs every stage a PR row runs, Release
# included, so any stage's result on a branch has a baseline to be read
# against. Pin full commits, never branch names: a branch moves, and evidence
# about a moved branch is evidence about nothing. Keep this file and
# The branch column is what makes a stale pin visible rather than something to
# remember: it names the branch (on origin, without the `origin/` prefix) whose
# tip the pin is meant to be, which for a PR row is the PR's head branch. It
# cannot be inferred, because a pin sits on many branches (baseline on every
# branch cut from main; a PR's commit on every PR stacked on it).
# `v1-qualification.sh --check-pins` fetches and exits non-zero when any pin is
# not its branch's tip, and every run records the same check in each row's
# identity.txt and in SUMMARY.md. Repinning means moving the commit column to
# the branch's new tip, and keeping the handoff's commit list in step.
# pr116-with-119 composes two PRs and names only #119's head branch. #116's own
# branch (fix/capture-experience-reliability) is checked by hand: its tip must
